index_slide1_text: The adventure consists of visiting seven locations significant to the history and culture of Belgrade and Serbia.
index_slide2_text1: Each location is one task. Each task has two riddles:
index_slide2_li1: the first riddle reveals the next location
index_slide2_li2: the second riddle is solved at the location itself
index_slide3_text: To move to the next location, you must complete all requirements at the current one. No skipping!
index_slide4_text: The game is designed to challenge players to connect clues using information that cannot always be found on site. To succeed, you will need to rely on the internet, navigation, maps, and other online resources.
index_slide4_strong: We do not recommend using artificial intelligence — it takes away the charm of the game.
index_slide5_text: Enter your answers in the forms on the corresponding pages. If the answer is correct, you automatically advance to the next level.

nivo2_poem:
In the name of the place ahead
A hidden word lies still.
Replace it with the Turkish one,
And all becomes more clear.
nivo2_hint1: On Dorćol, old, counting centuries. Its tall tower rules the whole end. There the barefoot pray to God. A place of peace and prayer, in the heart of the city.
nivo3_poem:
Ninety-nine stars with eight bright rays,
Shining on three sides, light never fades
Each bears the name of a god and human virtues.
Three numbers await your wisdom:
The first stands where summer dwells,
The second shines where dawn breaks.
The third rests where the day settles,
Write them all, let secrets be no more.
nivo3_hint1: Enter the mosque and look around.
nivo3_hint2: The numbers are connected to the cardinal directions.
nivo3_hint3: South, east, west — look at the walls, use navigation for directions.
nivo4_poem:
Where once a Turkish cemetery rested,
Later many people gathered at the market.
An infamous prison once stood there
Where temples of knowledge now grace the city.
nivo4_hint2: Faculty of Chemistry, Faculty of Philology, Faculty of Philosophy
nivo5_poem:
Beneath the one who stands alone,
Where no gate guards his stone,
A hidden secret waits below.
Look to the one who wished to know,
Who learned from ages long gone by,
And watched the centuries pass him by.
nivo5_hint2: Обрати пажњу на текст у подножју

nivo6_poem:
An eternal wanderer through the world and knowledge,
He turned his life into a quest for discovery.
So follow his path and seek the answer.
And when you reach the place where the journey ends,
where his name rests in silence,
let his final trace be your sign:
where his rest lies — the next step is hidden.
nivo6_hint1: Interpret the meaning of “where the journey ends”
nivo6_hint2: The place where Dositej found his eternal rest
nivo7_poem:
One writer asks for whom I toll so strong,
another cries that no treasure surpasses the book.
The first seeks me in the hour of death and war,
the second drives me from the gates of enlightenment.
My name alone shall not reveal the way,
but silent signs I carry shall guide your gaze.
From ages past I bear two marks within,
one identifies me, the other defies the years.
Seek not one alone, nor follow only the other,
let them speak together of what they have guarded for so long.
nivo8_poem:
Where words become a song at night,
and ancient stones keep tales untold,
where night outlasts the morning light,
the bohemian spirit still takes hold.
Seek not the tower, nor royal gate,
nor bells that call the faithful through.
Where wine and verse once sealed their fate,
the next hidden path awaits for you.
nivo8_hint2: Follow the gaze of Đura Jakšić
nivo8_hint3: The house of a great man
nivo8_hint4: Count the symbols on the plaque
nivo9_poem:
A famous poet, cast in bronze,
Still keeps his timeless watch.
Where his steadfast gaze is fixed,
Your next step shall be revealed.
There, great names call the past to life,
While silent symbols guard a hidden message.
nivo9_hint4: Count the occurrences of the letters in the text
nivo9_hint6: The 6th, 24th, 20th, and 1st letters of the Serbian alphabet
nivo10_title: THE ONE WHO POINTS THE WAY
nivo10_poem:
Beside the treasury of days long past,
Near the house where countless stories dwell,
Of stone and bronze it proudly stands,
Guarded by cities on either hand.

nivo12_poem:
Where once the stone was shaped by hand,
A flame of faith and history still stands.
Under the shadow of the cross and bells,
Time walks slowly where eternity dwells.
Read carefully the stone and the silence it keeps,
The next hidden truth in its memory sleeps:
A king and a patriarch found their rest here,
Its ancient monastery gave it a likeness dear.

nivo2_location: The Castle of Despot Stefan Lazarević was located in the Upper Town of the Belgrade Fortress. Despot Stefan received Belgrade under his administration in 1403. The city then became the capital of the Serbian state. The castle served as the residence of the despot and his court. It was surrounded by strong stone walls. It had several towers and gates. The most important was the Keep Tower (Donjon Tower). The castle was designed to withstand enemy attacks. It contained the ruler's private chambers. Both local and foreign envoys were received there. At that time, Belgrade was an important military and trading center. After Despot Stefan's death in 1427, the city was returned to the Kingdom of Hungary. Over the following centuries, the castle was almost completely destroyed. Today, only its archaeological remains have survived. A bronze scale model of the castle can be seen at Kalemegdan. The model shows what the castle looked like in the 15th century. The model was created by sculptor Kolja Milunović. It was unveiled on July 17, 2014. It stands near the site where the original castle once stood. Thanks to the model, visitors can imagine the former appearance of Despot Stefan's capital.
nivo3_location: The Bajrakli Mosque is the only surviving mosque in Belgrade. It is located in Gospodar Jevremova Street, in the old part of the city. It was built between 1660 and 1688 during Ottoman rule. It was originally known as the Čohadži Mosque. It received the name Bajrakli in the 18th century. The name comes from the Turkish word "bayrak," meaning flag. A flag was raised from its minaret to signal the time for prayer. The mosque was built in the classical Ottoman style. It has one dome and one minaret. Its walls are made of stone and brick. The interior is decorated with simple Islamic ornaments. Like all mosques, it is oriented toward Mecca. During Austrian rule, it was temporarily converted into a Catholic church. After the Ottomans returned, it became a mosque once again. Today, it is the main Islamic place of worship in Belgrade. It has been declared a cultural monument of great importance. It has been restored several times due to damage throughout history. It is open to both worshippers and visitors who respect its rules. It is an important part of Belgrade's cultural heritage. The Bajrakli Mosque stands as a reminder of the long and diverse history of the Serbian capital.
nivo5_location: Students' Square is one of the oldest and most important squares in Belgrade. It is located in the very center of the city, between Dorćol and Kalemegdan. Throughout history, this area has changed its appearance and purpose many times. During Roman times, a part of the ancient city of Singidunum was located here. In the Middle Ages, the area was near important roads and settlements. During the Ottoman period, a Turkish marketplace was located here. In the 19th century, the Great Market was situated on this spot. Later, the area was transformed into a square. The famous Glavnjača prison, the detention center of the Belgrade City Administration, was located here. During the 19th and early 20th centuries, criminals as well as political opponents of the authorities were imprisoned there. The Glavnjača building stood on the site of today's Faculty of Chemistry of the University of Belgrade. The building of the Great School, the first institution of higher education in Serbia, was also located on Students' Square. The Great School was founded by Dositej Obradović in 1808. Today, the building of the University of Belgrade Rectorate stands on that site. A monument to the scientist Josif Pančić is also located on the square. The remains of Roman buildings are preserved beneath the square. Today, Students' Square is an important place for education and culture. It represents a place where different periods of Belgrade's history meet.
nivo6_dositej: Dositej Obradović was one of the most important Serbian educators and writers. He was born around 1739 in Čakovo in Banat. His real name was Dimitrije Obradović. In his youth, he became a monk and received the name Dositej. Later, he left monastic life and dedicated himself to learning. He traveled across Europe and became familiar with the ideas of the Enlightenment. He learned foreign languages and gained knowledge in various fields. He supported the education of the people and the spread of knowledge. He believed that education should be available to everyone. He wrote the famous work "The Life and Adventures". Dositej strongly supported the use of the Serbian vernacular language in literature. In 1808, he founded the Great School in Belgrade. It is considered the predecessor of the University of Belgrade. After the liberation of Serbia, he participated in creating new educational institutions. He became the first Minister of Education in Serbia. He was a friend and associate of Vuk Karadžić. He died in 1811 in Belgrade. His monument is located at Students' Square in Belgrade. Dositej's work left a great mark on Serbian culture and education. Today, he is considered one of the most important figures in Serbian history.
nivo7_location: The Cathedral Church of Saint Michael the Archangel is one of the most important churches in Belgrade. It is located in the very center of the city, near Kalemegdan. It was built between 1837 and 1840 during the reign of Prince Miloš Obrenović. It was designed by the architect Adam Friedrich Kwerfeld. The church was built in the Classical style with Baroque elements. Its tall bell tower is one of the recognizable symbols of old Belgrade. The interior of the church is decorated with a richly crafted iconostasis. The iconostasis was created by the famous Serbian painter Dimitrije Avramović. The church was an important gathering place for the Serbian people during the 19th century. Numerous rulers and high-ranking church officials were crowned or buried there. The church contains the graves of Prince Miloš Obrenović and Prince Mihailo Obrenović. Metropolitan Mihailo and Patriarch Gavrilo are also buried there. The graves of Dositej Obradović and Vuk Karadžić are located in the churchyard. The building of the Patriarchate of the Serbian Orthodox Church is located nearby. The Cathedral Church has been one of Belgrade's important spiritual centers for centuries. It has been restored several times throughout its history. It was particularly damaged during the bombing of Belgrade in the First World War. Today, the Cathedral Church is an active Orthodox place of worship and an important cultural monument. Its churchyard is one of the most significant historical sites in old Belgrade. The Cathedral Church bears witness to the period when the modern Serbian state was being established.
nivo9_location: Skadarlija (officially — Skadarska Street) is one of the most famous old streets in Belgrade. It is located in the very center of the city, near Terazije and Republic Square. Its history dates back to the first half of the 19th century. The street was named after the city of Shkodër (Skadar in Serbian), which is now in Albania. It was once a poor street of craftsmen on the outskirts of old Belgrade. At the end of the 19th century, artists and writers began moving there. Skadarlija gradually became the bohemian center of Belgrade. Poets, actors, painters, and journalists gathered in its traditional taverns. Among the famous bohemians who spent time in Skadarlija were Đura Jakšić and Jovan Jovanović Zmaj. Đura Jakšić lived in one of the houses in Skadarlija. His house is now one of the symbols of the street. Famous taverns such as "Three Hats," "Two Deer," and "My Hat" were located in Skadarlija. Artists and visitors gathered there over wine, music, and song. The street is known for its cobblestones, old houses, and distinctive atmosphere. At the beginning of the 20th century, Skadarlija became one of the favorite places of Belgrade's cultural life. Today, it is one of the most visited tourist streets in Belgrade. Visitors can listen to traditional urban music and try traditional Serbian dishes here. Skadarlija has preserved part of the spirit of old Belgrade. Because of its bohemian tradition, it is often called the Montmartre of Belgrade.
nivo11_location: Republic Square is one of the most famous squares in Belgrade. It is located in the very center of the city, where several important streets meet. The square began to take shape after part of the city walls was demolished in the 19th century. The Stambol Gate once stood on this site. The gate was one of the main entrances to Belgrade during Ottoman rule. It was demolished in 1866 on the orders of Prince Mihailo Obrenović. After the gate was demolished, the area was gradually transformed into a square. The square was named Republic Square after Serbia became a republic in 1945. In the center of the square stands a monument to Prince Mihailo Obrenović. The monument was created by the Italian sculptor Enrico Pazzi. It was unveiled in 1882 and has become one of the symbols of Belgrade. Prince Mihailo is depicted on horseback, pointing towards southern Serbia. The National Museum of Serbia is also located on the square. Opposite the museum stands the National Theatre, which opened in 1869. The square has long been an important gathering place for the people of Belgrade. Celebrations, protests, and public gatherings have been held here. Today, it is one of the busiest places in central Belgrade. Knez Mihailova Street, the city's main pedestrian zone, begins at the square. Republic Square connects important historical, cultural, and tourist sites in Belgrade. For this reason, it is one of the places visited by almost every visitor to the city.
nivo13_location: The Church of Saint Mark is one of the most famous Orthodox churches in Belgrade. It is located in Tašmajdan Park, near the city center. The present church was built between 1931 and 1940. It was designed by architects Petar and Branko Krstić. It was built in the Serbian-Byzantine style, inspired by the Gračanica Monastery. The church is dedicated to Saint Mark the Apostle and Evangelist. Its exterior is decorated with red and yellow stone. A large dome dominates the appearance of the church. The interior of the church has never been completely finished. A large marble iconostasis is one of its most notable features. The iconostasis was created by the sculptor Dragomir Arambašić. The church contains the relics of Emperor Dušan, brought from the Monastery of the Holy Archangels near Prizren. The tomb of Patriarch German is also located inside the church. King Alexander Obrenović and Queen Draga are buried here as well. The church was damaged during the bombing of Belgrade in the Second World War. It has been restored several times throughout its history. Today, it is one of the most important Orthodox churches in Belgrade. Its architecture and history attract many visitors. Together with Tašmajdan Park, it forms one of the most recognizable landmarks in central Belgrade. The Church of Saint Mark is an important part of Belgrade's spiritual and historical heritage.
intro_11: Peace and good fortune be upon you, wayfaring traveller.
intro_12: I am the chronicler of old Belgrade, guardian of its memory.
intro_13: Once, I would record all that befell this city: its days of glory and its days of sorrow, the names of the renowned and the deeds of the forgotten.
intro_21: But time scattered my chronicle. Its pages were strewn across the city like autumn leaves, and with them, its memory began to fade.
intro_22: Fate has brought you here. Find the lost pages and restore the city's story.
intro_23: Only when the final page is returned to its place will the chronicle be whole once more.
